claims.text: A machine-learning model can predict an optimum severe-plastic-deformation processing window.
The model is trained on experimental data covering strain rate, temperature, pressure, and composition.
The predicted SPD window can simultaneously preserve phase stability and refine the microstructure.
Simultaneous phase stabilization and microstructure refinement will optimize mechanical and functional properties.
The target starting materials have coarse grains and metastable phases.
Severe plastic deformation or rapid consolidation performed under model-selected conditions will produce the proposed effects.
The relevant processing window occurs at ambient or moderately elevated temperatures with controlled strain rate and pressure.
Model-guided processing produces a refined and homogeneous microstructure with a stable phase distribution.
The resulting stable phase distribution suppresses excessive grain growth and undesirable phase transformations.
The machine-learning model integrates multiscale experimental and processing data.
Data-driven optimization can identify a narrow processing window that balances grain refinement and phase stability during SPD.
Model-guided treatment will yield ultrafine, stable grains.
Ultrafine, stable grains will improve strength, ductility, and functional properties relative to conventional processing.
Conventional thermomechanical processing often compromises phase stability or causes unwanted grain coarsening.
The approach is effective primarily within a specific processing window.
Model efficacy may decline outside the conditions represented in its training data.
Transferability of the model across different alloy systems has not been established.
Prediction accuracy and robustness depend on the quality and breadth of the training dataset.
